_note: Hand-derived from the Wikipedia Description text captured in species.raw.json. Each entry keeps the source sentence so every colour is traceable and correctable. null = the article does not state that colour; the matcher drops the trait rather than guessing.

Amanita muscaria.capSource: The bright red cap ranges from 5-30 centimetres in diameter.
Amanita muscaria.stemSource: The stipe is white, 5-20 cm high by 1-2 cm wide.

Amanita phalloides.capSource: The color of the cap can be pale-green, yellowish-green, olive-green, bronze, or (in one form) white.
Amanita phalloides.stemSource: The stipe is white with a scattering of grayish-olive scales.

Lanmaoa asiatica.capSource: It is reddish in color and an ectomycorrhizal symbiote of Pinus yunnanensis.

Psilocybe cubensis.capSource: The cap is brown becoming paler to almost white at the margin and fades to more golden-brown or yellowish with age.
Psilocybe cubensis.stemSource: The hollow white stipe is 4-15 cm high.

Agaricus bisporus.capSource: The pileus or cap of the original wild species is a pale grey-brown, with broad, flat scales on a paler background.

Psilocybe semilanceata.capSource: When it is moist, the cap is ochraceous to pale brown to dark chestnut brown, but darker in the center.
Psilocybe semilanceata.stemSource: The slender yellowish-brown stipe is 4.5-14 cm long.

Boletus edulis.capSource: The fruit body has a large brown cap which can reach 30 cm in diameter.

Coprinus comatus.capSource: The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
Coprinus comatus.stemSource: The white and fairly thick stipe measures 6-40 cm high.

Pleurotus ostreatus.capSource: In the wild, it ranges from white to gray or brown; the margin is inrolled when young.

Armillaria ostoyae.capSource: It can be distinguished from other Armillaria species by its cream-brown colors, prominent cap scales, and a well-developed ring.

Flammulina filiformis.capSource: The cap surface is smooth, viscid when damp, ochraceous yellow to yellow-brown.
Flammulina filiformis.stemSource: Pale yellow at the apex, yellow-brown to dark brown towards the base.

Chlorophyllum molybdites.capSource: The cap is whitish in colour with coarse brownish scales.

Coprinopsis atramentaria.capSource: The greyish or brownish-grey cap is furrowed, initially bell-shaped, and later more convex.
Coprinopsis atramentaria.stemSource: The stipe measures 5-17 cm high by 1-2 cm thick, is grey in colour, and lacks a ring.

Psilocybe cyanescens.capSource: A hygrophanous pileus (cap) that is caramel to chestnut-brown when moist, fading to pale buff when dried.
Psilocybe cyanescens.stemSource: The stem (which is white when undisturbed).

Psilocybe azurescens.capColorName: chestnut to ochraceous brown to caramel
Psilocybe azurescens.capSource: It is chestnut to ochraceous brown to caramel in color, often becoming pitted with dark blue or bluish black zones.

Leucocoprinus birnbaumii.capSource: The surface is lemon yellow to sulphur yellow, smooth or slightly powdery and covered in ragged, fibrous scales.

Grifola frondosa.capSource: The caps are grayish-brown, often curled or spoon-shaped, with wavy margins and 2-10 cm broad.
Grifola frondosa.stemSource: The cream-coloured stipe (stalk) has a branchy structure.

Galerina marginata.capSource: Pale to dark ochraceous tawny over the disc and yellow-ochraceous on the margin, fading to dull tan when dry.
Galerina marginata.stemSource: Below the ring it is brown down to the reddish-brown to bistre base.

Amanita caesarea.capSource: This mushroom has an orange to red cap, initially hemispherical before convex and finally flat.

Astraeus hygrometricus.capSource: The spore case is sessile, light gray to tan color and 1 to 3 cm broad; the rays are dark grey to black.

Tremella fuciformis.capSource: The fruit bodies are gelatinous, watery white, up to 7 centimetres across.

Inonotus obliquus.capSource: It is a sclerotium or mass of mycelium, mostly black because of a substantial amount of melanin.

Hydnellum peckii.capSource: The cap is initially whitish, but later turns slightly brownish, with irregular dark-brown to nearly black blotches.

Auricularia auricula-judae.capSource: The upper surface is a reddish-tan-brown with a purplish tint and finely pilose.

Pleurotus eryngii.stemSource: The whitish stem is 3-10 cm tall and 1-3 cm wide.

Agaricus campestris.capSource: The cap is white, may have fine scales, and is 3 to 12 centimetres in diameter.
Agaricus campestris.stemSource: The stipe is 3 to 10 cm tall, predominantly white and bears a single thin ring.

Cantharellus cibarius.capSource: Cantharellus cibarius is the golden chanterelle, the type species of the chanterelle genus.

Phallus impudicus.capSource: Topped with a conical cap covered with the greenish-brown slimy gleba.
Phallus impudicus.stemSource: Inside this is a white structure called the receptaculum.

Armillaria mellea.capSource: Armillaria gemina lacks the yellow cap background; the organism blooms honey mushrooms.

Coprinellus micaceus.stemSource: The stipe surface is at first velvety with a very fine whitish powder.

Amanita pantherina.capSource: Deep brown to hazel-brown to pale ochraceous brown, densely distributed warts that are pure white to sordid cream.
Amanita pantherina.stemSource: The stipe is 5-15 cm long, subcylindric, white, becoming slightly tannish in age.

Lactarius indigo.capSource: The cap surface is indigo blue when fresh, but fades to a paler grayish- or silvery-blue.

Lactarius deliciosus.capSource: Lactarius deliciosus has a carrot-orange cap that is convex to vase shaped.
Lactarius deliciosus.stemSource: It has a squat orange stipe that is often hollow, 2 to 8 cm long.

Phallus indusiatus.capSource: Its reticulated surface is covered with a layer of greenish-brown and foul-smelling slime, the gleba.
Phallus indusiatus.stemSource: The hollow stalk is white, roughly equal in width throughout its length.

Ganoderma lucidum.capSource: Reishi is a purple-brown mushroom with a long stalk, brown spores, and a fan-shaped cap with a shiny appearance.
Ganoderma lucidum.stemSource: The stipe is tawny to russet colored and 1.5 times the diameter of the cap.

Tuber melanosporum.capSource: The round, dark brown fruiting bodies have a black-brown skin with small pyramidal cusps.

Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.capColorName: chestnut or orangish brown to pearly cream
Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.capSource: Chestnut or orangish brown to yellowish brown to pearly cream color, hygrophanous, glabrous.
Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.stemSource: During youth the cap is dark brown/black (the stem is white).

Cordyceps militaris.capSource: The fungus forms 1-8 centimetres high, club-shaped and orange/red fruiting bodies.

Clathrus archeri.capSource: Coated in spore-bearing gleba on the upper surface which is dark greenish-brown in colour.

Amanita virosa.capSource: It is able to be peeled and is white, though the centre may be ivory.
Amanita virosa.stemSource: The crowded, free gills are white, as is the stipe and volva.

Laetiporus sulphureus.capSource: Its fruit bodies grow as striking golden-yellow shelf-like structures on tree trunks and branches.

Panaeolus foenisecii.capColorName: brownish when moist, tannish when dry
Panaeolus foenisecii.capSource: Hygrophanous with a brownish colour when moist and tannish when dry, often with a dark band around the margin.
Panaeolus foenisecii.stemSource: The stipe is 3 to 8 cm, fragile, hollow, beige to light brown, fibrous.

Psilocybe mexicana.capColorName: ocherous to brown or beige to straw
Psilocybe mexicana.capSource: Ocherous to brown or beige to straw color in age, conic to campanulate or subumbonate.
Psilocybe mexicana.stemSource: Stipe: straw color to brownish or reddish-brown, becoming darker where injured.

Gyromitra esculenta.capSource: The cap is brownish, and can variously be shaded reddish, chestnut, purplish, or golden.
Gyromitra esculenta.stemSource: Perched on a stout white stipe up to 6 cm high.

Clathrus ruber.capSource: The dark olive-green to olive-brown, foul-smelling sticky gleba covers the inner surface of the receptacle.

Panaeolus cinctulus.capSource: Striking cinnamon-brown when moist, soot-black when wet.
Panaeolus cinctulus.stemSource: The stipe is reddish brown or covered by whitish powder, hollow.

Amanita bisporigera.capSource: The cap surface is smooth and white, sometimes with a pale tan- or cream-colored tint in the center.
Amanita bisporigera.stemSource: The white stipe is 6-14 cm by 0.7-1.8 cm thick, solid.

Omphalotus olearius.capSource: A poisonous orange gilled mushroom; Omphalotus olearius is the same shade of orange internally and externally.
Omphalotus olearius.stemSource: If the jack-o'-lantern's stem is peeled, the same shade of orange as the outer flesh.

Psilocybe tampanensis.capSource: Ochraceous brown to straw brown, buff to yellowish-grey when dry, with slight bluish tones at the margin.

Paxillus involutus.capSource: May be reddish-, yellowish- or olive-brown in colour and typically 4-12 cm wide.

Amanita ocreata.capSource: The rest of the fungus below the cap is white; occasionally parts may have pinkish tones.
Amanita ocreata.stemSource: Bearing a thin white membranous ring until old age.

Craterellus cornucopioides.capSource: The upper and inner surface is black or dark gray, and rarely yellow.

Schizophyllum commune.capSource: The caps are 1-4 centimetres wide with white or grayish hairs.

Marasmius oreades.capSource: It is dry, smooth, pale tan or buff (occasionally white), or reddish tan.

Fomes fomentarius.capSource: The upper surface is tough, bumpy, hard and woody, varying in colour, usually a light brown or grey.

Hypomyces lactifluorum.capSource: Turning them a reddish orange color; at maturity the reddish orange H. lactifluorum thoroughly covers its host.

Tuber magnatum.capSource: The flesh is pale cream or brown with white marbling.

Amanita verna.capSource: The fool's mushroom is pure white, all the way to the gills and the stipe.
Amanita verna.stemSource: The caps, stipes and gills are all white in colour.

Morchella esculenta.capSource: The cap is pale brownish cream, yellow to tan or pale brown to grayish brown.
Morchella esculenta.stemSource: The stem is white to pallid or pale yellow, hollow.

Omphalotus illudens.capSource: Desarmillaria tabescens forms small, dull orange caps.

Suillus luteus.capColorName: chestnut, rusty, olive brown or dark brown
Suillus luteus.capSource: The cap is chestnut, rusty, olive brown, or dark brown in color with a diameter of 4-10 centimetres.
Suillus luteus.stemSource: Below the ring, the stipe is dingy white, sometimes streaked with brownish slime.

Sarcoscypha coccinea.capSource: The inner surface of the cup is deep red (fading to orange when dry) and smooth.
Sarcoscypha coccinea.stemSource: The stipe is stout and up to 4 cm long, and whitish, with a tomentum.

Imleria badia.capSource: Imleria badia fruit bodies have a chestnut to dark brown cap.

Auricularia heimuer.capSource: The upper surface is finely tomentose, coloured fawn to reddish brown when fresh.

Entoloma hochstetteri.capSource: The cap colour is indigo-blue with a green tint, and is fibrillose.

Russula emetica.capSource: It is a bright scarlet or cherry red, and in maturity the margins have fine radial grooves.
Russula emetica.stemSource: The white stem measures 4.5-10.5 cm long by 0.7-2.4 cm thick.

Ganoderma applanatum.capSource: The upper surface of the fruiting body appears brown, covered with reddish-brown.

Collybia nuda.capSource: One whose gills and cap are initially light violet and mature to burgundy.

Craterellus tubaeformis.capSource: The mushroom is mostly yellow with a grayish-brown cap.
Craterellus tubaeformis.stemSource: The mushroom is mostly yellow with a grayish-brown cap.

Cerioporus squamosus.capSource: The body can be yellow to brown and has squamules or scales on its upper side.

Cortinarius violaceus.capSource: The specific epithet violaceus refers to the deep violet colour of its cap.
Cortinarius violaceus.stemSource: The stipe is a similar colour to the cap, and covered in wool-like fibrils.

Shaggy parasol.capSource: A large and conspicuous agaric, with thick brown scales and protuberances on its fleshy white cap.

Tremella mesenterica.capSource: The lobes translucent, deep yellow or bright yellow-orange, fading to pale yellow.

Hypholoma fasciculare.stemSource: The stipe is 3-12 cm tall and 3-10 mm wide, light yellow, orange-brown below.

Rubroboletus satanas.capColorName: greyish white to silvery-white or buff
Rubroboletus satanas.capSource: When young, the pileus is greyish white to silvery-white or buff.

Stropharia rugosoannulata.capSource: A reddish-brown convex to flattening cap up to 30 cm across.
Stropharia rugosoannulata.stemSource: The firm flesh is white, as is the tall stem, which bears a wrinkled ring.

Gymnopilus junonius.capSource: It is bright yellow-orange in younger specimens and orange-brown or reddish brown in older ones.

Lycoperdon perlatum.capSource: It is off-white with a top covered in short spiny bumps or jewels.
Lycoperdon perlatum.stemSource: It has a stem-like base, and is whitish before browning in age.

Coprinopsis lagopus.capColorName: pale to very dark-brown beneath a silvery grey veil
Coprinopsis lagopus.capSource: The color of the cap surface is pale to very dark-brown at center beneath the whitish to silvery grey veil.
Coprinopsis lagopus.stemSource: The stem is whitish in color, and is hollow, hairy over the whole surface.

Flammulina velutipes.capSource: The cap is light orange, darker toward the center.
Flammulina velutipes.stemSource: The flesh of the cap is yellow, while that of the stem is brown.

Aleuria aurantia.capSource: The orange fruiting body is 1-10 centimetres wide, cup-shaped, externally fuzzy.

Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca.capSource: The species has a golden-orange cap ranging from 2-10 cm in diameter.
Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca.stemSource: The orange stipe is 1.5-8 cm tall and 0.5-1 cm thick, and lacks a ring.

Hydnum repandum.capSource: The orange-, yellow- or tan-colored pileus (cap) is up to 17 centimetres wide.
Hydnum repandum.stemSource: The stipe is either white or the same color as the cap, and is sometimes off-center.

Xylaria polymorpha.capSource: The fruiting bodies can be 3-10 centimetres tall, externally colored black or brown.

Scleroderma citrinum.capSource: The fruit bodies grow to 10 centimetres broad and 6 cm high with a yellowish peridium, or outer skin.

Fomitopsis betulina.capSource: The fruit bodies are pale, with a smooth greyish-brown top surface.

Pholiota squarrosa.capSource: The cap color is yellowish-brown to tawny in older specimens.

Psilocybe caerulipes.stemSource: The stipe is 3-6 cm long, tough, and is whitish to brown at first.
